VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 /
Sarama Resources Ltd. ("
Sarama
" or the "
Company
provides an update on its arbitration proceedings against the Government of Burkina Faso and the commencement of reconnaissance drilling by Riedel Resources Limited ("
Riedel
") at the Cosmo Gold Project ("
Cosmo
") in Western Australia.
Highlights
Arbitration progressing towards the Merits Hearing scheduled for 22-26 February 2027, with the Government of Burkina Faso's Rejoinder due on 1 December 2026
Damages sought updated to US$245.3 million plus interest. The Company's independent quantum expert assessed the total claim, including pre-award interest, at US$326.8 million as at 31 July 2026
Riedel commenced reconnaissance drilling at Cosmo on 1 November 2026 - the first drilling at the project in more than 30 years
Sarama retains exposure to exploration success through its approximate 32% equity interest in Riedel, with scope to increase to 44% upon achievement of defined milestones
Sarama's Executive Chairman, Andrew Dinning commented:

"Arbitration continues to progress towards the February 2027 hearing in line with the Procedural Timetable, and the updated damages assessment and continuing accrual of interest underscore the significance of the claim for Sarama and our continued focus on recovering value for shareholders.

At Cosmo, it is pleasing to see Riedel commence drilling to test targets generated by Sarama's soil geochemistry programs and targeting work. Our substantial shareholding in Riedel provides continued exposure to exploration success while reducing Sarama's funding requirements and helping to preserve shareholders' exposure to any potential arbitration award."
Arbitration Proceedings

Sarama's arbitration against the Government of Burkina Faso arises from the unlawful expropriation of its Tankoro 2 Exploration Permit, the central component of the Company's multi-million-ounce Sanutura Gold Project. The proceedings were commenced in December 2024 through the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes ("
ICSID
") under the Canada-Burkina Faso Bilateral Investment Treaty ("
BIT

Following the filing of Sarama's Memorial in October 2025 and the Government's Counter-Memorial in March 2026, the parties completed Document Production in June 2026. Sarama filed its Reply and Counter-Memorial on Jurisdiction on 31 July 2026, updating the damages sought to US$245.3 million, plus interest. The Company's Independent Quantum Expert, Accuracy London, assessed the total claim, including pre-award interest, at US$326.8 million as at that date. Interest continues to accrue.

The Government's Rejoinder is due on 1 December 2026. The Procedural Timetable remains substantially unchanged, with the Merits Hearing scheduled for 22-26 February 2027. At the hearing, the parties will present their cases and supporting evidence to the Tribunal, including the examination of witnesses. The date for the Final Award has not been determined.

Sarama continues to be represented by Boies Schiller Flexner (UK) LLP, a leading international law firm with extensive experience in investor-state arbitration and a strong track record in the natural resources sector with non-recourse funding provided by Locke Capital II LLC.
Riedel Commences Drilling at Cosmo
Riedel commenced reconnaissance drilling at the Cosmo Gold Project ("
Cosmo
") on 1 November 2026, marking the first drilling at the project in more than 30 years. The program is targeting gold-in-soil anomalies identified by earlier sampling programs (
refer to Riedel news release dated 4 November 2026

Cosmo comprises approximately 580km² of tenure along more than 50km of the Cosmo Newbery Belt in Western Australia's Laverton region. Sarama's soil geochemistry programs defined extensive gold-in-soil anomalies and multiple priority targets, with heritage clearance received in June 2026 enabling subsequent drilling.
Sarama completed the sale of its Cosmo and Mt Venn Projects (together, the "
Projects

") to Riedel in July 2026 in exchange for shares, performance rights and reimbursement of certain Project-related expenses. The transaction resulted in Sarama acquiring an approximate 32% equity interest in Riedel, with scope to increase to approximately 44% if all performance rights vest and are exercised, based on Riedel's capital structure at completion.
The transaction allows the Projects to advance through Riedel, while Sarama retains substantial exposure to their future success.
